Action Plan:
1. Provide acute migraine management today: advise simple analgesics (Paracetamol) or compound analgesic (Co-codamol, dose/route/frequency not documented) plus non-steroidal anti-inflammatory (Ibuprofen or Naproxen, dose/route/frequency not documented).  
2. Instruct patient to keep a detailed headache diary (timing, triggers, medication use, response) until follow-up next week.  
3. Safety-net: return urgently if headache worsens or persists >2–3 days, fails to respond to medication, or if new red-flag symptoms arise (neck pain, focal weakness, visual change, vomiting, fever).  
4. Offer reassurance regarding low likelihood of brain tumour; outlined reasons and provided red-flag education.  
5. Schedule follow-up appointment in one week to:  
   a) review headache diary and symptom course;  
   b) consider prophylactic migraine therapy if frequency persists;  
   c) review suitability of current combined oral contraceptive in the setting of migraine with aura and discuss alternative contraception.  
6. Recommend stress-reduction strategies (regular exercise, breaks at work) and review at next visit.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Acute left-sided throbbing headache beginning today at mid-day.  
• History of presenting illness:  
  – Pain preceded by zig-zag visual lines and blurred vision in both eyes (visual aura) a few minutes before headache onset.  
  – Throbbing, unilateral (left) pain; worsened by bending forward or moving head/neck.  
  – Associated photophobia (wearing sunglasses indoors), nausea, and two episodes of vomiting.  
  – No fever, no rash, no speech difficulty, no limb weakness, no balance problems, no head trauma.  
  – Similar episode a few weeks ago lasting ~2 days, resolved with rest and analgesics.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses; never formally diagnosed with migraine.  
• Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill – Microgynon (dose/route/frequency not documented), started 3 months ago.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Family history: Mother – migraines and hypothyroidism; no family brain tumours.  
• Social history: Works in high-stress fashion industry, lives alone; non-smoker, no alcohol, no regular exercise.

Objective:
• No vitals or neurological examination findings documented in transcript.  
• Patient reports afebrile; denies focal neurological deficits.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute unilateral headache with visual aura  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Migraine with visual aura (DDx likelihood: High).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Medium) – positional component, recent estrogen OCP use.  
     • Intracranial mass / brain tumour (Low) – vomiting & positional pain but acute onset and normal neuro exam oppose.  
     • Viral meningitis (Low) – photophobia but no fever or neck stiffness.  
   – Investigations planned: None today; will reconsider neuro-imaging or further work-up if red-flag features develop or headaches increase in frequency.  
   – Treatment planned: Paracetamol, Co-codamol, and NSAIDs (Ibuprofen/Naproxen) as required; headache diary; consider prophylactic therapy at follow-up.

2. Health anxiety regarding brain tumour  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Health anxiety related to headache.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Generalized anxiety disorder vs situational stress.  
   – Treatment planned: Education on migraine features vs tumour, provision of red-flag list, reassurance; encourage return if concerns persist.  
   – Relevant referrals: Consider psychological support or counselling if anxiety continues (to be assessed at follow-up).

3. Combined oral contraceptive (Microgynon) review  
   – Assessment / likely concern: Estrogen-containing OCP in patient now presenting with migraine with aura (potential contraindication; CVST risk).  
   – Differential diagnosis: CVST (Medium) as alternative explanation for headache.  
   – Plan: Discuss risks/benefits and alternative contraception at next week’s review; monitor for thrombotic symptoms; low threshold for imaging if headache pattern changes.

4. Occupational stress / lifestyle factors  
   – Assessment: Work-related stress possibly contributing to headache frequency or severity.  
   – Plan: Advise regular exercise, stress-management techniques; reassess coping strategies at follow-up.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: allergies not elicited; no documented vitals or focused neurological/ophthalmic examination; medication doses/routes/frequencies absent.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minor repetitions but overall intelligible.
